capture.final_message:
Use the presentation of `CategoryTheory.Quotient`: its morphisms are `Quot` classes of morphisms of `C` modulo `HomRel.CompClosure`.

- For the first conjunct, apply the quotient-morphism induction principle to `f`. It suffices to consider a representative morphism `g : x ⟶ y` from `C`; the induced quotient morphism is exactly `Quotient.functor.map g`, so the hypothesis `h g` proves the required predicate. The key intermediate goal is thus `P (Quotient.functor.map g)` for each representative `g`.

- For the second conjunct, unfold the inverse on the quotient groupoid. It is defined on a representative class `[f]` by sending it to `[f⁻¹]`. Hence
  `Quotient.inv (Quot.mk _ f) = Quot.mk _ (Groupoid.inv f)`
  follows directly from the defining equation for `Quotient.inv` (possibly after a small simplification).

The essential mechanism is that `CompClosure` is stable under the groupoid inverse, which is what makes the second representative-level definition well-defined; this is already built into the quotient groupoid construction.
